quotes.passage: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
quotes.statement: The paper proposes a network architecture, the Transformer, that relies only on attention mechanisms and does not use recurrence or convolutions.

quotes.passage: We show that this approach can effectively solve complex RL tasks without access to the reward function, including Atari games and simulated robot locomotion, while providing feedback on less than 1% of our agent’s interactions with the environment.
quotes.statement: The authors state that learning from non-expert human preferences between pairs of trajectory segments can solve complex RL tasks, including Atari games and simulated robot locomotion, without access to the reward function, and the paper reports feedback on less than 1% of the agent's interactions.

quotes.passage: I have perforce analyzed the matter from my own perspective; given my own conclusions and done my best to support them in limited space.
quotes.locator: MIRI reprint, PDF p. 2, §1 Introduction, para. 3
quotes.statement: In the MIRI reprint of the 2008 chapter, the author states that he has analysed the global catastrophic risks of artificial intelligence from his own perspective and set out and supported his own conclusions.

quotes.passage: We introduce our first-generation reasoning models, DeepSeek-R1-Zero and DeepSeek-R1.
quotes.statement: The paper introduces two reasoning models, DeepSeek-R1-Zero and DeepSeek-R1, which it calls its first-generation reasoning models.

quotes.passage: To support the research community, we open-source DeepSeek-R1-Zero, DeepSeek-R1, and six dense models (1.5B, 7B, 8B, 14B, 32B, 70B) distilled from DeepSeek-R1 based on Qwen and Llama.
quotes.statement: The authors state that they release DeepSeek-R1-Zero, DeepSeek-R1 and six dense models distilled from DeepSeek-R1 on Qwen and Llama bases as open source.

quotes.passage: We call these models foundation models to underscore their critically central yet incomplete character.
quotes.statement: The report names models trained on broad data at scale and adaptable to many downstream tasks "foundation models", explaining the term by their "critically central yet incomplete character".

quotes.passage: This report provides a thorough account of the opportunities and risks of foundation models, ranging from their capabilities … to their applications (e.g., law, healthcare, education) and societal impact (e.g., inequity, misuse, economic and environmental impact, legal and ethical considerations).
quotes.statement: The report describes itself as an account of the opportunities and risks of foundation models, covering capabilities, technical principles, applications and societal impact.

quotes.passage: We report the development of GPT-4, a large-scale, multimodal model which can accept image and text inputs and produce text outputs.
quotes.statement: The report describes the development of GPT-4, which it presents as a large-scale multimodal model that accepts image and text inputs and produces text outputs.

quotes.passage: We evaluate a collection of such models (with between 244M and 137B parameters) on two new benchmarks, MBPP and MathQA-Python, in both the few-shot and fine-tuning regimes.
quotes.statement: The paper evaluates large language models of 244M to 137B parameters on program synthesis in Python using two benchmarks it introduces, MBPP and MathQA-Python, in few-shot and fine-tuning settings.

quotes.passage: To diagnose the failures of current models and support research, we introduce GSM8K, a dataset of 8.5K high quality linguistically diverse grade school math word problems.
quotes.statement: The paper introduces GSM8K, a dataset it describes as 8.5K grade school math word problems.

quotes.passage: To increase performance, we propose training verifiers to judge the correctness of model completions.
quotes.statement: The paper proposes training verifiers that judge the correctness of model-generated solutions.

quotes.passage: In this work, we focus on a suite of 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks which we call BIG-Bench Hard (BBH).
quotes.statement: The paper defines BIG-Bench Hard (BBH), a suite of 23 BIG-Bench tasks, and studies chain-of-thought prompting on it.

quotes.passage: In this work, we develop and release Llama 2, a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) ranging in scale from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters.
quotes.statement: The authors state that they develop and release Llama 2, a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned large language models from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters.

quotes.passage: We present the Natural Questions corpus, a question answering data set.
quotes.statement: The paper presents the Natural Questions corpus, a question answering data set built from queries issued to the Google search engine.

quotes.passage: We present TriviaQA, a challenging reading comprehension dataset containing over 650K question-answer-evidence triples.
quotes.statement: The paper presents TriviaQA, a reading comprehension dataset that it reports contains over 650K question-answer-evidence triples.

quotes.passage: This paper explores the ability of language models to generate a coherent chain of thought—a series of short sentences that mimic the reasoning process a person might have when responding to a question.
quotes.statement: The paper studies prompting language models to generate a chain of thought, a series of intermediate sentences before an answer, and reports that this improves reasoning performance in sufficiently large models.

quotes.passage: We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously.
quotes.statement: The paper presents a residual learning framework intended to ease the training of substantially deeper neural networks.

quotes.passage: GPipe is a scalable pipeline parallelism library that enables learning of giant deep neural networks.
quotes.statement: The paper presents GPipe, a pipeline parallelism library for training very large deep neural networks across accelerators.

quotes.passage: Here we use recent advances in training deep neural networks … to develop a novel artificial agent, termed a deep Q-network, that can learn successful policies directly from high-dimensional sensory inputs using end-to-end reinforcement learning.
quotes.statement: The paper presents an agent, the deep Q-network, that learns policies directly from high-dimensional sensory inputs through end-to-end reinforcement learning.

quotes.passage: This work bridges the divide between high-dimensional sensory inputs and actions, resulting in the first artificial agent that is capable of learning to excel at a diverse array of challenging tasks.
quotes.statement: The paper states that its agent is the first artificial agent capable of learning to excel at a diverse array of challenging tasks.

quotes.passage: We introduce LLaMA, a collection of foundation language models ranging from 7B to 65B parameters.
quotes.statement: The paper introduces LLaMA, a collection of language models from 7B to 65B parameters trained, it states, on publicly available datasets only.

quotes.passage: We release all our models to the research community
quotes.statement: The authors state that they release all the models to the research community.

quotes.passage: In this paper, we introduce the task of physical commonsense reasoning and a corresponding benchmark dataset Physical Interaction: Question Answering or PIQA
quotes.statement: The paper introduces a physical commonsense reasoning task and a benchmark dataset for it, Physical Interaction: Question Answering (PIQA).

quotes.passage: We outline a high-level research direction to solve the agent alignment problem centered around reward modeling: learning a reward function from interaction with the user and optimizing the learned reward function with reinforcement learning.
quotes.statement: The paper outlines a research direction for the agent alignment problem based on reward modeling, in which a reward function is learned from interaction with the user and then optimized with reinforcement learning.

quotes.passage: We propose Iterated Amplification, an alternative training strategy which progressively builds up a training signal for difficult problems by combining solutions to easier subproblems.
quotes.statement: The paper proposes Iterated Amplification, a training strategy that builds a training signal for difficult problems by combining solutions to easier subproblems.

quotes.passage: We propose a benchmark to measure whether a language model is truthful in generating answers to questions.
quotes.statement: The paper proposes a benchmark, TruthfulQA, for measuring whether a language model is truthful in answering questions, and reports that it comprises 817 questions in 38 categories.

quotes.passage: The key idea is to randomly drop units (along with their connections) from the neural network during training.
quotes.statement: The paper presents dropout, a technique against overfitting that randomly drops units and their connections from a neural network during training.

quotes.passage: We show that dropout improves the performance of neural networks on supervised learning tasks in vision, speech recognition, document classification and computational biology, obtaining state-of-the-art results on many benchmark data sets.
quotes.statement: The authors report that dropout improved neural network performance on supervised tasks in vision, speech recognition, document classification and computational biology.

quotes.passage: We present a method for detecting objects in images using a single deep neural network.
quotes.statement: The paper presents a method, named SSD, for detecting objects in images with a single deep neural network.

quotes.passage: We call the resulting system R-CNN: Regions with CNN features.
quotes.statement: The paper presents R-CNN, an object detection system combining bottom-up region proposals with convolutional neural network features.

quotes.passage: We show that the answer is yes, and that the resulting system is simple, scalable, and boosts mean average precision, relative to the venerable deformable part model, by more than 40% (achieving a final mAP of 48% on VOC 2007).
quotes.statement: The paper reports that a convolutional network trained for ImageNet classification can be adapted to detect objects in PASCAL, with a mean average precision of 48% on VOC 2007.

quotes.passage: Caruana and his collaborators [1] have shown that it is possible to compress the knowledge in an ensemble into a single model which is much easier to deploy and we develop this approach further using a different compression technique.
quotes.statement: The authors state that they extend earlier work by Caruana and collaborators on compressing an ensemble's knowledge into a single model, using a different compression technique.

quotes.passage: We also introduce a new type of ensemble composed of one or more full models and many specialist models which learn to distinguish fine-grained classes that the full models confuse.
quotes.statement: The paper also introduces an ensemble of full models and specialist models that learn to distinguish fine-grained classes the full models confuse.

quotes.passage: In this work, we propose LIME, a novel explanation technique that explains the predictions of any classifier in an interpretable and faithful manner, by learning an interpretable model locally around the prediction.
quotes.statement: The paper proposes LIME, an explanation technique that explains the predictions of any classifier by learning an interpretable model locally around a prediction.

quotes.passage: In this work we address the task of semantic image segmentation with Deep Learning and make three main contributions that are experimentally shown to have substantial practical merit.
quotes.statement: The paper presents DeepLab, a semantic image segmentation system, and states three contributions: atrous convolution, atrous spatial pyramid pooling and the combination of convolutional networks with a fully connected CRF.

quotes.passage: Second, we propose atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) to robustly segment objects at multiple scales.
quotes.statement: The paper proposes atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) for segmenting objects at multiple scales.
